subject.title: feat: apply messages.responsePrefix to message tool outbound sends

question: Should `message(action="send")` inherit the current agent attempt's provider/model/thinking context for `messages.responsePrefix` templates, and what should happen when no live attempt context exists?
rationale: Current main deliberately skips unresolved model/provider/thinking templates to avoid sending raw placeholders, but the remaining requested behavior requires deciding whether cross-target tool sends should use the current source run context, target-session context, or no selected-model context.

options.title: Use current-attempt context
options.body: Pass the selected provider/model/thinking from the active agent run into message-tool sends so visible tool delivery matches direct replies when a live attempt exists, with a documented no-context fallback.

options.title: Keep static and identity only
options.body: Document that message-tool sends support static and identity prefixes but do not support selected-model variables because the send path does not perform model selection.

options.title: Move to broader attribution design
options.body: Track provider/model/thinking visibility under the broader model-attribution work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33975 and keep this issue limited to the already-merged static prefix behavior.

recommendation.title: Use current-attempt context
recommendation.body: Pass the selected provider/model/thinking from the active agent run into message-tool sends so visible tool delivery matches direct replies when a live attempt exists, with a documented no-context fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged partial implementation and documented the unresolved model/provider/thinking scope boundary in the fix history.
